notes.meaning: A good reputation based on godly character is far better than expensive perfume. Costly oils smell pleasant for a little while, but a faithful life leaves a lasting legacy. For those who belong to God, the day of death brings freedom from earthly toil, making it better than the day they entered this troubled world.

Visiting a home where people are grieving does more good for the soul than going to a noisy feast. At a funeral, everyone is reminded that earthly life must end in death. Facing this truth helps the living think about eternity instead of wasting their days on empty pleasures.

Honest sorrow teaches deeper lessons than careless laughter. A sad face often goes with a heart that is being softened, humbled, and drawn closer to God. Wise people dwell on serious matters like death and eternity, while foolish people only hunt for constant amusement.

Listening to honest correction from a wise person hurts at first, but it brings lasting help. In contrast, the wild laughter and songs of fools are like dry thorns burning under a pot—they crackle loudly and blaze up fast, but vanish just as quickly. Shallow flattery and noisy fun leave nothing of real value behind.

Cruel oppression can drive even a sensible person to act rashly or lose self-control. In the same way, accepting a bribe blinds a person's judgment and ruins their integrity. Greed and unjust power can easily spoil good character if one is not on guard.

How a matter finishes is far more important than how it starts. Pride makes people impatient and eager to boast, but quiet patience sees hardships through to a good outcome. Waiting on God through difficult trials proves to be far better than rushing ahead in self-reliance.

People should not allow anger to flare up quickly in their spirits. While anyone might feel a sudden burst of temper, a fool welcomes resentment and lets it make a permanent home in his chest. Holding onto bitter fury harms the person who harbors it and shows a lack of wisdom.

Constantly complaining and wishing for the good old days is not wise. Every generation has its share of hardships as well as God's kindness. Longing for an imagined golden past often springs from an ungrateful heart that fails to see God's daily mercies in the present.

Wisdom is an excellent possession, just like an inheritance of land or money, and it brings great benefits to the living. Wealth can provide a shelter from some of life's troubles, but wisdom offers a much greater defense. True godly wisdom preserves and protects a person's very life.

People should look closely at how God rules the world. No human being has the power to straighten out what God in His sovereignty has decided to make crooked. Accepting that God is in complete control helps believers stop fighting His providence.

When good days arrive, believers should enjoy them with thankful hearts. When hard days strike, they should remember that God has allowed both prosperity and trouble. He balances life in this way so people realize they cannot control the future and must rely fully on Him.

In this broken world, life does not always seem fair. Sometimes an upright person dies young despite doing good, while a wicked person lives to an old age in the middle of their sin. Seeing such confusing things reminds us that life on earth does not always reveal God's final justice.

This warning cautions against self-righteous pride and harsh scrupulosity. Trying to appear holier than others or setting up strict rules beyond God's commands only leads to exhaustion and downfall. True godliness is humble and does not parade its own goodness.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars read the phrase 'destroy yourself' as meaning 'be astonished,' taking this as an observation of the shock a righteous person feels when an unfair world cuts life short rather than as a rule against strict holiness.

notes.meaning: No one should assume that because the wicked sometimes live long, it is safe to plunge into evil. Living in wild, reckless sin often leads to disaster and cuts life short. Foolish rebellion provokes God and brings people to an early grave.

It is vital to hold onto the warnings against both self-righteous pride and wild rebellion. The person who truly fears God will avoid these destructive traps. Deep reverence for the Lord provides the humility and obedience needed to stay on the right path.

Godly wisdom provides a person with greater strength and security than ten military rulers guarding a city. Armies and weapons can easily fail, but understanding helps a person handle dangerous crises. Living wisely protects a leader better than physical force.

There is not a single person on earth who does only good and never commits a sin. Even the best and most faithful people still fail and fall short of God's perfect law. Realizing that everyone is flawed keeps believers humble and dependent on God's grace.

People should not try to listen to every word spoken about them, or they might hear their own servant speaking ill of them. Conscience quickly reminds us that we have also spoken harsh, unkind words about other people. Remembering our own faults helps us show grace and overlook thoughtless remarks.

The Teacher tested everything with his great mind, determined to master all wisdom, but found it was beyond his reach. The deep truths of God and the universe are too vast for any human being to fully uncover. Acknowledging our limited understanding is a key part of true wisdom.

The Teacher devoted his full attention to exploring reality and discovering the reasons behind how things happen. He especially wanted to uncover the sheer stupidity of wickedness and the madness of foolish choices. Examining sin shows that disobeying God is utter folly that leads nowhere good.

Falling into the grasp of an alluring, deceitful woman brings a bitterness worse than death itself. Her heart acts like a hunter's net and her arms are like heavy chains that pull people away from God. Only the person who pleases God through faithful obedience will escape, while careless sinners are trapped.

After weighing facts one by one, the Teacher came to a painful discovery. Among a thousand royal advisors, he found only one upright man, but among the many foreign women of his royal court, he found none who were faithful and virtuous. Living among flatterers and idolatrous companions showed how hard it is to find genuine godliness in corrupt surroundings.

The grand summary of the search is that God originally made human beings upright, innocent, and good. The misery and corruption seen everywhere come from mankind's choice to invent selfish schemes and wander into sin. Our broken condition is not God's fault, but the result of humanity turning away from His design.
